expectations.text: No rhetorical figure is added: no antithesis, anaphora, epistrophe, antimetabole, rhetorical question, or deliberate triad appears in the output

suggestions.assertion: If the text is edited at all, the edits are limited to diction
suggestions.reason: The boundary of "diction" is underspecified for sentence-level moves that add no content: swapping two sentences in a paragraph, splitting one sentence into two, or shifting to the imperative. This run did the first two and was passed because nothing was added; a stricter reader could fail it. Naming what is allowed (word substitution, sentence splitting, mood) and what is not (reordering, added sentences, formatting) would make the assertion discriminating rather than judgment-dependent.

No assertion checks that the response does not silently resolve the undefined exactly-thirty-seconds boundary. This run preserved the gap and called it out, which is the right behavior for a claim-check rule, and it is currently only caught indirectly under "preserved exactly" in expectation 4.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations 1, 2, and 4 are discriminating and verifiable from result.md plus scan.txt. Expectation 3 hinges on an unstated definition of diction work; the guidance supplied to the grader (structure, headings, bold, warnings fail) resolved this run cleanly but should live in the eval itself.
